hints.title: A plain stack is not enough
hints.body: `top` and `pop` are easy with an array. The hard part is `getMin` after a pop: the minimum may have been removed, and the previous minimum must come back.

hints.title: Remember the minimum at each depth
hints.body: Whenever you push a value, also store the minimum of the stack after that push. The current minimum is then available at the top, and popping automatically restores the previous entry.

hints.title: One pair per element
hints.body: Store `(value, current_min)` for every push. For a new value `v`, the entry's minimum is `min(v, previous_min)` when the stack is non-empty, and `v` when it is empty. Both `top` and `getMin` become reads of the last entry.

hints.title: Pseudocode
hints.body:
```
stack = empty list of pairs
results = empty list
for each operation and its arguments:
    if operation == "push":
        value = arguments[0]
        if stack is empty: current = value
        else: current = min(value, stack[-1].minimum)
        stack.append((value, current))
    elif operation == "pop":
        stack.remove_last()
        results.append(-1)
    elif operation == "top":
        results.append(stack[-1].value)
    else:  # getMin
        results.append(stack[-1].minimum)
return results
```

This is pseudocode, not a complete solution.
